speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) due to prematurity at 33 weeks gestation.

The clinical picture of respiratory distress occurring within hours of birth in a preterm infant, accompanied by respiratory acidosis and hypoxemia, is highly suggestive of surfactant deficiency. The normal white blood cell count makes an infectious etiology like sepsis less likely at this stage. Based on the gestational age and presentation, the most probable diagnosis is Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).
